items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: And so Bill Grauer and those people, they were part of it, they were the fundamental start.

ctx.x: Okay. This might have been after you left Hamilton but there was a short lived renewed interest in Dixieland and hot music. Do you recall when that — I believe it was in the early to mid-50s.

Yeah. Well that’s when the stuff was coming out of New Orleans. And there was that revival. Look magazine went down there and filmed, and of course the dean of them all was Bill Russell and his American music. And there were other people who were — I’ve forgotten his name now but he had the Icon label. So there was a renaissance. And of course actually there was the Commodore Music Shop. Now I went to the Commodore Music Shop when they were on the downtown side of 42nd Street. Later on that building was gutted…
